newsitem.title: POLAND: Daiwa advises overweight stance on Polish stocks.
newsitem.headline: Daiwa advises overweight stance on Polish stocks.

text.p: Daiwa Europe Ltd recommended an overweight position in Polish stocks, saying in its September report the market remained undervalued despite an 84-percent rise since the start of the year.
The London-based securities house said in its monthly report on Central and Eastern Europe.
It said it had nudged up its year-end WIG index target to 16,000 from over 15,000. On Thursday the WIG closed at 14,454 points.

"We still believe Polish shares deserve an overweight allocation in a regional portfolio as, increasingly, investors compare this bourse with others in developed Europe and conclude it is still cheap," it said.
It said it recommended a 20-percent weighting for Poland in the central and Eastern European portfolio, double the market's current 10.2 percent share of regional capitalisation.
Daiwa said it still considered a few of the listed banks attractive, but said their recent run-up made most of them fairly valued, except for BPH.
It said it still favoured several of the construction- related companies such as Prochem, Mostostal Warszawa and Mostostal Export.
It said two companies, which did not have convincing business strategies or well-defended sectors of activity were Exbud and Optimus.
